title: DCVA repair: identify the double-check assembly before parts work
description: DCVA repair is a device-specific check-valve service decision.
prompt: How should a double-check valve assembly repair be scoped?
answer: DCVA repair is a device-specific check-valve service decision. The model, size, installed orientation, failed check finding, and required retest define the work—not the phrase double check alone.
urgency: Escalate uncertain device identification, damaged body or shutoffs, high-hazard questions, or any proposed change to the required protection type.
diagramAlt: Backflow service and compliance workflow reference
identifiers: Confirm the nameplate identifies the actual double-check assembly and nominal size.
Record which check or test finding failed instead of using only a pass-fail label.
Verify whether the governing program requires a specified protection level or approved assembly.

choices.label: I have a notice or program requirement
choices.detail: Use the issuing program to verify deadline and filing requirements.

choices.label: The assembly failed or needs service
choices.detail: Document the device and define repair plus retest scope.

choices.label: I manage a commercial asset
choices.detail: Separate access, shutdown, testing, and closeout responsibilities.

steps.title: Establish the exact record
steps.body: Keep the certified test finding and full-device label together before repair pricing.

steps.title: Define the specific scope
steps.body: Use manufacturer documentation for the exact assembly and distinguish internal parts from body or piping work.

steps.title: Prove the closeout
steps.body: Schedule and retain the required post-repair test and report submission confirmation.

safeChecks: Do not infer a kit from another double-check product family.
Keep shutoff and test access conditions in the scope.
Check with the authority before changing assembly type.
stopConditions: The device type or degree-of-hazard requirement is uncertain.
The body, shutoffs, or piping need work outside the internal repair scope.
notThisDevice: A generic service listing does not establish program eligibility.
A device family is not enough to identify compatible parts.
This page does not replace a qualified assessment or authority approval.
evidenceNote: Use the governing utility or authority requirement and exact manufacturer documentation to validate this specific decision path.
